structured.approach:
Attempt 4 fixes both G1 refusals in feat.prototype. I re-read both contracted inputs and the current output first. The complete feat.prototype file is on disk; I applied the fixes to it as targeted edits rather than writing the file again.

(1) SD-1 row: the "Why" cell said "No secrets or personal data in outputs (G8)" and cited record:brief. Neither the step brief nor any input mentions G8 or such a rule. The cell now reads "Keeps real vendor and contact data out of a design artefact (agent judgement)", and the source is "agent judgement".

(2) Synthetic data attribution: the section 6 intro now says that the workbook action in the brief names "synthetic data rules" but that neither the brief nor any input defines them. That is the only fact the brief supports. SD-1 to SD-6 are stated as agent judgement and raised as PQ-P5. The prompt-basis row "Synthetic data only" now says the same.

A grep confirms that no G-gate ID remains in the output. Each remaining record:brief citation matches text in the brief:
- trigger, owner, gate, outcome and inputs
- "Connectors approved for you: api:github"
- the workbook action wording

The design content is unchanged from attempt 3.

claims.text: The design library requires the overdue risk table to use class 'overdue-risk', each row to use class 'risk-high', 'risk-medium', 'risk-low' or 'risk-unknown', and the columns Invoice, Vendor, Days overdue and Amount (two decimals), and to render nothing when there are no rows. The prototype applies all four rules.
Figma is not connected in this test run, and the step brief lists api:github as the only approved connector. So the FigJam flow and the Figma Make prompt are delivered in text form.
The workbook action names synthetic data rules but does not define them. The synthetic data rules SD-1 to SD-6 in the prototype are agent judgement and are raised as PQ-P5.
The only UI surface in the PRD is renderOverdueRisk(rows) in ap_portal. It returns an empty string when there are no rows.
The wireframe lists only unpaid invoices more than 30 days past due. An unpaid invoice exactly 30 days past due is not listed, and paid invoices are excluded.
Rows are sorted by days descending, then by id. The ascending text order of id follows assumption P-A2, which is not yet confirmed (PQ-2).
A vendor with no entry in risk_by_vendor gets risk 'unknown', shown with the row class risk-unknown.
The risk level is shown only as the row class, with no visible Risk column, following AC-19 while OQ-B9 is open.
Amounts are two-decimal strings and are shown as received, never through a binary float, in line with AC-18, NFR-1 to NFR-3 and D-2026-044. How ap_portal formats them is left to the TRD under OQ-B10.
The risk label is advisory only. The user flow ends in a manual decision, and the prototype has no row actions.
The outcome of this step is Low Fidelity Wireframes, gated by the UX lead, triggered by PRD Reviewed, with PM as owner.
No conflict was found with D-2026-031, D-2026-044 or D-2026-050, or with the approved PRD.

open_questions: PQ-P1: Which visual tokens should style risk-high, risk-medium, risk-low and risk-unknown? The design library defines none.
PQ-P2: Which portal page hosts the overdue risk table, and where on that page?
PQ-P3: Are loading, error, pagination or long-list states needed? The PRD defines none.
PQ-P4: If risk stays as a row class only (OQ-B9), how is it made perceivable without relying on colour alone?
PQ-P5: Is there an approved synthetic data rule set for prototypes? The workbook action names one but no input defines it; SD-1 to SD-6 are agent judgement.
PQ-P6: Should Figma/FigJam be connected so the flow and prompt can be produced as Figma files?
PQ-P7: Should rows offer any manual action? The PRD defines none, so none is drawn.
Carried from feat.prd and still open: OQ-B1 to OQ-B10 and PQ-1 to PQ-6. Most relevant to this prototype: OQ-B2, OQ-B8, OQ-B9, OQ-B10 and PQ-2.
structured.summary: I updated feat.prototype for FEAT-ZD-48600 and fixed both G1 refusals. The SD-1 row no longer cites G8 or record:brief and is marked agent judgement. The synthetic-data attribution now says only that the workbook action names synthetic data rules without defining them. SD-1 to SD-6 are agent judgement and raised as PQ-P5. The rest of the prototype is unchanged: low-fidelity wireframes in text form, a FigJam flow, a Figma Make prompt, and a check against the PRD that found no conflict with the PRD or the decision log.
